desire_based_hook_formula.name: Desire-Based Hook Formula
desire_based_hook_formula.when: When creating hooks that need to trigger immediate emotional response
elements: Identify the core desire (freedom, status, money, safety, belonging)
Create contrast between current state and desired state
Open a curiosity loop around the gap
Promise the gap can be closed

attention_conversion_funnel.name: Attention-Conversion Funnel
attention_conversion_funnel.when: When structuring content that moves from attention to action
steps: Step 2: Retain — Promise value in the first 3 seconds
Step 3: Deliver — Give the promised value
Step 4: Convert — Aligned offer or CTA

illusion_of_novelty.name: Illusion of Novelty Framework
illusion_of_novelty.when: When making familiar topics feel fresh and new
illusion_of_novelty.method: Reveal a changed aspect of a familiar thing + tie it to an outcome the viewer wants
illusion_of_novelty.example: 'A new way to get a root canal with robotics — zero needles, zero pain, back to work in 30 minutes'

key_tactics: The first 1-3 seconds determine whether the viewer stays or scrolls
Specific numbers build credibility, vagueness on results creates suspense
Direct address ('you' or 'if you') makes it personal and relevant
Contrarian statements trigger cognitive dissonance — viewer must watch to see if you back it up
Curiosity gaps work best on educational and case study content
Pain-point-first hooks work for problem-aware audiences
Proof-first hooks work for skeptical audiences
